title: Lamentations 1
paragraphs: ¹ How deserted the city sits, once so full of people! She who was great among the nations is now like a widow. She who was a princess among the provinces has become a forced laborer. ² She weeps bitterly in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. Among all who loved her, there is none to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her — they have become her enemies. ³ Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh slavery. She lives among the nations but finds no resting place. All who pursued her have caught her in the narrow passes. ⁴ The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to her appointed feasts. All her gates are desolate. Her priests groan, her young women grieve, and bitterness is hers. ⁵ Her enemies have become her masters, her foes prosper — for the LORD has brought grief on her for the multitude of her sins. Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy.

⁶ From the daughter of Zion all her majesty has departed. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture — they have fled away without strength before those who pursue them. ⁷ Jerusalem remembers in the days of her affliction and wandering all the precious things that were hers in the days of old. When her people fell into the enemy's hands and there was no one to help her, her enemies looked on and laughed at her downfall. ⁸ Jerusalem has sinned greatly, and so she has become unclean. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away. ⁹ Her filthiness clings to her skirts; she gave no thought to her future. Her fall was astounding; there is no one to comfort her. "Look, O LORD, at my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed." ¹⁰ The enemy has stretched out his hands over all her treasures. She has seen the nations enter her sanctuary — those you commanded not to enter your assembly.

¹¹ All her people groan as they search for bread. They have traded their precious things for food to keep themselves alive. "Look, O LORD, and see how worthless I have become." ¹² "Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow — the sorrow inflicted on me with which the LORD has struck me in the day of his fierce anger. ¹³ From above he sent fire into my bones; he spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He has left me desolate, faint all day long. ¹⁴ The yoke of my transgressions is bound into a yoke; by his hand they were woven together. They have come upon my neck and sapped my strength. The LORD has handed me over to those I cannot withstand. ¹⁵ The LORD has rejected all my warriors in my midst. He summoned an army against me to crush my young men. The LORD has trampled the virgin daughter of Judah as in a winepress.

¹⁶ "For these things I weep; my eyes overflow with tears — because the comforter who could restore my spirit is far from me. My children are desolate because the enemy has prevailed." ¹⁷ Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has decreed for Jacob that his neighbors should become his enemies. Jerusalem has become like a menstrual cloth among them. ¹⁸ "The LORD is righteous, for I have rebelled against his word. Listen, all you peoples, and see my pain. My young women and young men have gone into captivity. ¹⁹ I called out to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and elders perished in the city while searching for food to keep themselves alive. ²⁰ See, O LORD, how distressed I am! My stomach churns, my heart is wrung within me, because I have been so rebellious. In the street the sword bereaves; in the house there is death."

²¹ "People have heard me groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that you have done it. Bring on the day you have announced, that they may become like me. ²² Let all their wickedness come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me for all my transgressions — for my groans are many and my heart is faint."
